newsitem.title: USA: US Midco prods fall with NYMEX, activity dries up.
newsitem.headline: US Midco prods fall with NYMEX, activity dries up.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot product prices for November barrels fell with NYMEX Friday and liquidity dried up as the market remained surprised by Thursday's decline, traders said.
"After yesterday, everybody sat back and wondered what was going to happen next," a trader said.
He said skittish traders sapped even more activity from Friday's market, which normally thins as traders step back to evaluate their needs for the following week.
December crude ended off 32 cents a barrel at $23.03, pulling down refined products.
Front-month heating oil settled 0.25 cent a gallon lower at 66.60 cents while Dec gasoline edged up 0.09 cent a gallon to 64.70 cents.
Differentials in Group Three and Midco turned mixed Friday.
Diffs for prompt unleaded gasoline in the Group climbed about 0.75 cent to end 3.75/4.00 cents over the screen. Outright prices for unleaded ranged 68.45/68.70 cents.
Meanwhile, outright prices between premium and conventional gasoline narrowed as premium's advantage eased 0.50 cent, leaving the regrade 2.75/3.00 cents.
Group Jet kero was 1.00/1.50 cents over December NYMEX heating oil, shedding a half cent from yesterday's diff.
But Chicago diffs for conventional gas fell, losing 0.25 cent to remain 3.50/3.75 over the NYMEX.
